limit-at-infinity.def: The value $f(x)$ approaches as $x$ grows without bound: $\lim_{x \to \infty} f(x) = L$ (or as $x \to -\infty$). A finite limit at infinity gives the horizontal asymptote $y = L$; these limits describe the end behavior of a function.

dominant-term.def: The term that grows fastest as $x \to \infty$ and so decides a limit at infinity. In the long run $\ln x$ grows slower than any positive power of $x$, a higher power beats a lower one, and $e^x$ beats every power.
